transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-16
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ravi (Redwood SE), Lucia (Redwood Product), Evan (Head of AI, Cascade), Priya (Platform Eng), Marco (FinOps), Tasha (Security)

Auto-summary (may be imperfect):
- Walked through Console route lens, per-route cost charts, and route split reports.
- Showed suggestions from Optimize (batching/quantization hints) and how that maps to cost delta.
- Discussed pilot and next steps: send pricing + security docs, run perf bench.

Transcript: (timestamps approximate, transcription imperfect)
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, can you hear me ok?
[00:05] Evan: Yep, loud and clear.
[00:07] Maya: Great. I'm Maya, I'm the account lead, with me is Ravi our solutions engineer and Lucia from product. Today we're gonna walk the Console cost lens, per-route dashboards, and go through a small pilot plan.
[00:20] Priya: Sounds good, we mostly want to see per-endpoint breakouts and how you attribute tokens to features.
[00:25] Ravi: Cool, that's exactly what we'll show. Quick note -- if you see any jargon or we say Redwood Dedicated or Redwood Private, shout out, we sometimes call them different things in docs.
[00:34] Marco: No worries. For context our main ask: we run a mix of chat and classification. Chat is 70% of tokens, classification is many short calls but high QPS. We need predictable cost and latencies under 200ms p95 ideally.
[00:48] Maya: Good, that's super helpful. Alright i'll share my screen -- sorry if the resolution's a bit fuzzy.
[00:55] [screen sharing begins]
[01:05] Ravi: Ok starting on the Console home. First card shows total spend last 30 days, token distribution, and a simple route map. Notice the route map groups by model and route name, so you can see which user-facing feature maps to which inference route.
[01:25] Priya: That route grouping is helpful, does that reconcile with our existing path naming? We have internal proxies so routes can be different.
[01:33] Ravi: Yes you can map route identifiers to your proxy paths. There's a small mapping file you drop in or via the API we ingest route tags. It isn't perfect in the auto-map step but you can correct mappings.
[01:45] Evan: The per-route cost column, is that taking into account KV cache hits? Because for chat we rely heavily on prefix caching.
[01:53] Ravi: Good call. The Console attempts to show effective tokens charged and shows cache hit rate as a metric on the route card. There's a caveat -- sometimes KV cache spelled as K-V cash or KV cache in agent transcripts, sorry -- but the data comes from runtime telemetry. For cached tokens we discount the token tally and it's visible as 'effective token' metric.
[02:14] Marco: Ok nice. Show the cost decomposition chart.
[02:18] Ravi: Sure -- here's the per-route cost waterfall. Top shows raw compute, then batching efficiency adjustments, then network egress and any model premium. The interesting slice is our Optimize recommendations which show a projected delta if you switch to a quantized variant or enable prefix caching aggressively.
[02:36] Priya: How does the Console estimate the delta for quantization? Our models are custom and quantization can change quality.
[02:42] Lucia: Right -- the recommendation engine uses historical token shapes and performance profiles from similar model families to estimate throughput and error bars. We always recommend a small eval set; the Console links to Eval playbooks so you can measure quality regression for each quantized config.
[02:57] Evan: Are those evals something you run in Redwood's cloud or do we run them internally?
[03:03] Lucia: You can do either. For a pilot we can run a shadow eval with sanitized prompts on our hosted infra, or we can give you the tooling to run locally with your private deployment. For compliance reasons many customers prefer running locally.
[03:16] Tasha: On compliance -- we need SOC2, SAML SSO, KMS integration, and also options for data residency. Do you support customer-managed KMS and a private control plane?
[03:26] Maya: Yes, Private deployment supports customer-managed KMS and a private control plane. We have SOC2 Type II and can share the certs. SSO via SAML/SCIM for RBAC is supported. We'll share the questionnaire.
[03:39] Tasha: Great. Also we have a requirement for audit logs at token-level for a subset of routes. Can the console surface token-level traces?
[03:48] Ravi: We surface token-level aggregates and per-request traces if you enable extended tracing. For private deployments you can ship full traces to your SIEM; for hosted we can pull them into an encrypted object store with limited retention. We'll discuss retention windows in the security docs.
[04:03] Marco: Back to costs: what's the delta between hosted and dedicated? Our finance team wants ballpark numbers with throughput tiers.
[04:11] Maya: I can share a pricing grid, but rough rules: hosted is usage-based with bit of premium for convenience; dedicated gives a fixed commit and usually lower per-token unit cost if you have consistent load. Dedicated also reduces variance and gives reserved GPU capacity which helps with p95 latency.
[04:27] Marco: Are there burst options? We have seasonal spikes.
[04:31] Ravi: Yes, Dedicated has configurable burst pools and overflow policies that route to hosted models as failover. You can control cost/latency trade-offs in the routing policy.
[04:41] Evan: Show the route-level SLO dashboard.
[04:44] Ravi: Here -- SLOs can be defined per-route, you can set p95 latency targets and max cost per 1k tokens. This panel shows p95 over time and annotations when a deployment roll or config change occurred.
[04:58] [timestamp jump]
[05:05] Priya: How granular is per-route telemetry? We want to split by org team and feature.
[05:11] Ravi: You can tag routes with team and feature labels; dashboards let you slice by tag. We also show attribution to calling services and user-provided metadata so you can do chargeback.
[05:22] Marco: Is the cost allocation deterministic? We sometimes see sampling in our tracing which skews numbers.
[05:28] Ravi: We do sampling for traces to reduce volume, but cost attribution is deterministic because it's tied to counted tokens and model run metadata. Sampling only affects deep request-level traces, not cost.
[05:38] Evan: Can you demo a real route and drill down?
[05:42] Ravi: Yep -- selecting the 'chat-concierge' route. You can see traffic heatmap, token distribution, average response length, and cost per 1k. There's also a histogram of sequence lengths -- helps pick kernel/serving profile.
[05:58] Priya: The histogram looks like our chat tails longer than we thought, we might be able to trim context.
[06:02] Lucia: Exactly, Console flags routes with heavy context and suggests prefix caching or short-term memory pruning to reduce effective tokens.
[06:10] Tasha: A question on data residency: if we want EU-only, can you pin a region and ensure logs and telemetry stay in the region?
[06:18] Maya: Yes, region pinning is supported in both Dedicated and Hosted tiers with enterprise controls; for Private it's customer-managed. There are slight differences in backup retention and support windows per-region. We'll include the region matrix in the doc pack.
[06:30] [07:15] [Ravi demonstrating a CSV export]
[07:20] Ravi: You can export the per-route cost CSV with breakdown columns: route_id, model_variant, raw_tokens, effective_tokens, cache_hits, compute_secs, cost_usd, team_tag. This is handy for your chargeback scripts.
[07:34] Marco: Can that export be auto-scheduled to an S3 bucket?
[07:37] Ravi: Yes, scheduled exports to S3 or to your GCS are supported. Encryption options tied to customer KMS can be applied.
[07:45] Priya: On the Optimize recommendations, is there an API to pull a suggested config so we can run it through our infra-as-code?
[07:53] Lucia: Yes, there's an API that emits recommendations as JSON with confidence scores. You can programmatically accept or stage them as feature flags.
[08:02] Evan: Do you support canary deploys across model variants? We want to roll quantized variants gradually.
[08:07] Ravi: Absolutely -- you can do weighted rollouts, percent traffic to each model variant, and automatic rollback on quality regressions if you hook up eval traces.
[08:18] Evan: Excellent. Marco, any finance-specific questions?
[08:21] Marco: One: how do you price multitenant plugins we use? We sometimes have partner models inline.
[08:28] Maya: Partner or third-party model premiums are surfaced separately. If you're invoking external models we show a per-call surcharge and label the cost. You can route them to a separate billing ledger.
[08:40] [09:00] Priya: A weird corner case: some of our classification calls are single-token but extremely high QPS, do you recommend pooling or sharding?
[09:09] Ravi: For many small calls we recommend batching or micro-batching, and sometimes a smaller quantized model with a GPU-optimized kernel. The Console's 'throughput profiler' will show expected p50/p95 under different batch sizes so you can pick the most cost-efficient config.
[09:25] Priya: Can we set automatic batching rules per-route?
[09:28] Ravi: Yes, you can set a max latency threshold and desired batch window; the runtime does continuous batching while respecting route SLOs.
[09:36] Evan: Any tradeoff to watch? Sometimes batching improves cost but worsens tail latency.
[09:41] Ravi: Right, that's the classic tradeoff. Console shows projected latency increase per-batch-window; you can tune at route-level.
[09:49] Lucia: And Optimize includes recommended quantization + batch profiles with a cost/time delta.
[09:55] [10:30]
[10:32] Marco: Let's talk about the pilot. Our goal is to validate cost savings and p95 under 200ms for primary chat route with 2m messages/day.
[10:40] Maya: Proposed pilot: 2-week pilot, shadow traffic replay of a sanitized 48-hour window, run two configs: hosted with standard model, hosted with quantized variant + Optimize suggestions, and optionally a Dedicated small pool to compare. We'll produce a side-by-side cost & quality report.
[10:55] Evan: For the shadow replay, we will redact PII and share a sample traffic export. Priya will lead that.
[11:02] Priya: Yep, we'll prepare sample and share secure link. How do we get the replay tool?
[11:07] Ravi: We'll give you a replay runbook plus a small container to run locally if you prefer, or we'll run it in a staging Redwood account with logs encrypted. Lucia: we'll also attach the Eval playbook to measure quality delta.
[11:18] Tasha: On runbook, add a section for data handling and where telemetry goes.
[11:22] Maya: Noted. We'll include explicit steps and retention.
[11:26] Marco: Anything else on security?
[11:28] Tasha: Just to confirm: for hosted pilot, do you persist raw prompts?
[11:33] Ravi: For hosted pilot we can set a no-persist policy for raw prompts; we'll only keep aggregates unless you opt-in. For Dedicated or Private you control storage.
[11:41] Evan: Great. Quick question: competitor angle. We tested a vendor who had faster p50 but token accounting was opaque. How is your token accounting validated?
[11:51] Ravi: We provide token-level counters, and you can reconcile with your client-side token counts. We also publish runtime telemetry to let you cross-check compute seconds and model variant used per call.
[12:02] Marco: Ok that helps.
[12:05] [small cross talk]
[12:12] Maya: Ok wrapping up, I want to recap next steps. We'll send pricing and a pilot template, Ravi will send perf benchmark runbook and we'll aim to run the benchmark next Wed. Cascade will share sample traffic and security requirements. Tasha will be the security point.
[12:30] Priya: One scheduling note: Marco wants an internal finance sync before committing to Dedicated. We'll aim to get the benchmark results and then do a finance review.
[12:40] Maya: Sounds good. Any final questions?
[12:44] Evan: No, thanks all. Looks promising.
[12:47] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email.
[12:51] [call ends]

Notes about transcription: occasional mis-hearings (K-V cache -> KV cache; Redwood Dedicated sometimes verbalized as Redwood Dedicato), filler words, and slight speaker mis-attribution in places.
